youtube.title: machine — filthy mechanical industrial rock, one chord, no mercy
youtube.description:
Industrial rock instrumental: filthy, mechanical, 120 BPM straight 4/4 in E minor, on one chord for the whole track. Distorted kit, corroded bass, saturated synths and texture doing the work harmony refuses to.

The groove is a physical loop and everything around it corrodes. Tension comes from density, drive, distortion, filtering and noise, never from a chord change. Each rebuild is more damaged than the last, and the ending is a burnout, not a resolution.

Written as text, mixed by measurement rather than by ear, rendered in the browser.

Chapters
0:00 The machine starts
0:16 Verse
0:32 Build and the first chorus
0:56 Breakdown and rebuild
1:28 Chorus 2
1:44 Chorus 3
2:00 Burnout

Play and edit this song in your browser at jonborchardt.github.io/strudel-bench — press play, drag a slider, change a note, hear it immediately. Nothing to install. 

Every song here is a text file. This one is songs/machine.strudel in the repo, along with the harness that plays it:
https://github.com/jonborchardt/strudel-bench

strudel-bench is a live-coding harness where a song is a text file written in a high-level language: parts, sections, and twelve musical axes (density, brightness, weight, space, articulation and so on) that a phrase like "darker and more spacious" can move. Most of the code and the songs were written by coding agents working from a written spec, in the spirit of my blog, "always shippable, always improving":
https://jonborchardt.github.io/blog/

The video is not a screen recording. It is generated from the song itself: every hit in the music drives the animation, and the world it plays in is chosen from the song's own musical features.

Built on Strudel, the JavaScript port of TidalCycles: https://strudel.cc
Samples come from the public Strudel packs, each under its own license: https://strudel.cc/learn/samples/

requests.ask: the music sounds flat and simplistic

changes.why: fixed riff 0 ~ 0 3@2 ~ 2 0 so every chorus hammers the same figure

requests.ask: add a -mixed version of arc, arrival, breakwater, cutwork, hunted and machine without altering the originals

changes.why: size .5 fade .15 damping 3500: one small dead room, the machine stays dry

the kit was the mix (1.7 dB under it, 8% of samples clipping); level does not move its peak (the kit saturates before the gain), so the rest came down and the clip share fell to .5%; a master limiter is not built
under the kick, ducked with a written 100 ms recovery
the sub pad peaked at full scale on its own; now ducked under the kick
the melody was 19 dB under the mix; now 10, foreground, a little right

requests.ask: use the new mixing tools on the -mixed songs: impulse-response rooms, humanize, compressor, depth words

changes.why: synthetic>room the generated small room cut to half a second (size .5 truncates the impulse): early reflections and a door, no tail; the machine stays dry
closer on the melody; no humanize anywhere, the machine is mechanical by design; no compressor, every part is dense

requests.ask: chorus 2 and 3 scratch and drop hits like other songs did; ensure we are not out of bounds

changes.why: width .8+ is jux, a doubled copy of every pad voice, each with a distortion worklet; under .8 the pad sweeps instead and the section's load falls
same: the doubled distorted pad was the load

this section ran ~46 voices at once with worklets and textures counted (the check read 22 before it counted them), the audio thread at 60-70% with the slowest callbacks over their deadline; now ~28, measured 48-57% busy

requests.ask: machine seems to clip: run it through the mix to keep it from clipping

changes.why: postgain 1>.4 the kit distorts (aggression) and superdough's distortion outputs tanh clamped to full scale whatever level fed it; postgain is the gain after it, so the kit's peak finally moves
postgain 1>.5 same: the bass distorts and shapes, level never moved its peak
postgain 1>.6 the sub pad distorts too; down with the rest
postgain 1>.8 a smaller cut keeps the hook foreground as the rest comes down
textures: drone postgain .5, stabs/grind/scream .6, bursts/squeals/breaths .7; the drone alone was a continuous saturated saw

requests.ask: machine still bad, way better but not close to good

changes.why: weight .95>.7 the bass sat an octave under its register at midi 16 (21 Hz): a rumble whose distortion harmonics were all anyone heard
register .15>.4 E2, out from under the kick's fundamental
notes: written lines ('0 0 7 0' in the choruses, '0 ~ 0 0' elsewhere) instead of the seeded line
aggression 1>.75 less of the distort .7 + shape .5 wall on the bass
sound sawtooth>square three raw saws in one section were mud; the bass keeps the saw
sound sawtooth>triangle same, and a softer grit under the distortion
weight 1>.7 no low voicing: a distorted low chord at E2 was mud under the bass
aggression 1>.8 less distortion on the chord
aggression .9>.75 distort .48 on 16th hats was fizz; weight 1>.85 less shape
postgain .8>.5 the melody had become the mix (2.4 dB under it)
duckDepth .3>.5 kick under bass: the duck is the fix the low-band lint asks for
textures: stabs and grind lose .coarse() (a worklet this page's bundle never defines: they had been silent) and distort .6/.5; drone .75>.5, scream .9>.6, squeals .7>.5

requests.ask: parts of chorus3 still break (2 spots)

changes.why: aggression .8>.5 the pad was 16 of chorus3's 47 nodes a step: eight overlapping chord tones each with a distortion worklet; no worklet on the busiest part
density .9>.7 fewer chord tones sounding at once; articulation .2>.4 a shorter release so chords do not pile up
weight .85>.5 no shape worklet on every kit hit; the gain it gave was x1.08

prompt: Filthy mechanical industrial rock at 120 BPM on one E minor chord, corroding textures stacked outside the axes
